clue.text: Tore label in shreds, and that shouldn't be allowed

indicators.note: to shred is to tear to pieces, so the three words before it are torn up and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rips a label to pieces, and a stickler protests that this is not permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in shreds' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is part of the fodder: TORE LABEL IN has the eleven letters needed, with 'shreds' alone as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbearable or past tolerating is exactly what ought not to be permitted.

clue.text: No sailors' fate

parts.note: taken as written
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors collectively

explanation.surface: A grim announcement that seamen have no destiny at all.
explanation.walkthrough: In Norse myth the Norns are the three goddesses who spin each person's destiny, matching the Fates of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology a Norn is one of the female beings who decide destiny, so one personifies fate.

clue.text: Shocking Russian river prospect

parts.note: the Ob is a great river of western Siberia
a prospect is a view, a scene

explanation.surface: A traveller finds a view of a Russian river startling.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent material is shocking to decency, the core sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Quits the day before new start is to be made

parts.note: the eve is the day before a festival or event

indicators.note: the start of the word new is its opening letter

explanation.surface: On the eve of a fresh beginning, two people agree to call it quits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quits' is the adjective, as in 'now we're quits': nobody owes anything. 'is to be made' only links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits means neither side owes the other, so the score is level.

clue.text: A town with more co-operation

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'A town with more co-operation (7)': AND (with) + OVER (more) gives ANDOVER, defined by 'A town', but 'co-operation' then has no job; no blog or database found to confirm the printed clue.

clue.text: Decree a quarter must be green

parts.note: a decree is an order with the force of law
north is one of the four quarters or cardinal points of the compass, abbreviated N

explanation.surface: An official order says a quarter of the town must be painted green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' is a noun here, a stretch of grass such as a village green.
explanation.definitionFit: A village green and a mown lawn are both open stretches of cut grass.

clue.text: Boring birds!

parts.note: reads as a complaint about dull birds, but means birds that bore holes into trees with their beaks

explanation.surface: A bored birdwatcher dismisses some species as dull.
explanation.definitionFit: These birds drill into tree trunks with their bills, so they literally bore.

clue.text: Appeared in casual wear — reprimanded for it

explanation.surface: Someone turned up in jeans and got told off for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing informally is one sense of the phrase; being scolded severely is the other, an idiom for a telling-off.

clue.text: The problem arising does cause confusion

indicators.note: a problem is something knotty to be worked out, so the letters of the next two words are tangled

explanation.surface: Whenever a difficulty crops up it sows confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' is the anagram signal on ARISING DOES; 'The' is only a link. 'does' looks like the verb of the sentence but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw something into disorder is to make it confused, removing its structure.

clue.text: Reckon a spring issue backed up the astrologer

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read from the bottom, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: to reckon is to work out a sum
to spring is to dart, move suddenly
a son is issue, offspring

explanation.surface: Someone tallies up a spring's flow, with the result endorsing a famous seer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed up' reverses the whole string SUM A DART SON, giving the name of the 16th-century French seer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostradamus was a French physician famed for his book of prophecies drawn from the stars.

clue.text: A number of bills for overnight accommodation

parts.note: four is a number
bills are posters stuck on walls, as in 'bill posting'

explanation.surface: A traveller notes several hotel bills paid for nights away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bills' suggests invoices for a hotel stay; it means posted notices.
explanation.definitionFit: These are grand beds with a post at each corner, a place to sleep for the night.

clue.text: There's no clamour from this once-revered figure

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means none
a din is a loud clamour

explanation.surface: A deity of old is said to make no noise at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The chief Norse god is no longer worshipped, hence 'once-revered'.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the chief god of Norse mythology, worshipped in former times but no longer.

clue.text: A small number turn in vain

parts.note: No. is the short form of number
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: A player gets only a few goes, and they are wasted.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-go plan is hopeless and futile, so efforts on it are wasted.

clue.text: Going on tiresomely, nod and grin foolishly

indicators.note: acting foolishly means acting without sense, so the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bore talks on while a listener nods and grins idiotically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two fodder words and is not part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A monotonous speaker drones, talking at length in a dull, humming way.

clue.text: Greek leader copied, being regarded with awe

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: A Greek chief was imitated and thus looked upon with reverence.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare open-mouthed is how one looks at something wonderful, in amazement.

clue.text: A person telling tales is really friendless subsequently

indicators.note: an ally is a friend, so being without one means the letters of that synonym are taken from the preceding word

parts.note: subsequently means later

explanation.surface: A gossip is, in the end, left without any friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friendless' tells you to remove ALLY (a friend) from REALLY, leaving RE.
explanation.definitionFit: One who relates something is a narrator, a teller of stories.

clue.text: Palindromic attribute

indicators.note: says the answer reads the same forwards and backwards, with nothing else to build

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A grammarian names a characteristic that reads the same both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attribute' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in 'refer a quote to Shakespeare'.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit something to a source, ascribing it, is to attribute it.

clue.text: The consumer shows some hesitation accepting a note

indicators.note: one word taking in the letters of the others means it surrounds them

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation in speech
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A shopper hesitates and then takes a banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who eats food consumes it.

clue.text: Potential fliers may well be hard-boiled

definitions.text: Potential fliers may well be hard-boiled

parts.words: Potential fliers may well be hard-boiled
parts.note: hard-boiled suggests tough characters such as pilots, but it is a cooking term for what a bird lays before its chicks can fly

explanation.surface: Would-be pilots are often tough customers.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhatched chicks are future birds, and they are often cooked hard in boiling water.

clue.text: Pole gone to get food of sorts

parts.note: S stands for the South Pole
ago means gone by, past

explanation.surface: A Polish man has left to buy something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a person from Poland; it is a compass pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A starch from palm pith, it is used in puddings and is one kind of foodstuff.

clue.text: Prize — money always

parts.note: L stands for the pound sterling, from Latin libra
ever means always

explanation.surface: A competition offers cash as its prize, and offers it every time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize' is the verb, prise (spelt prize in some usage): to force open.
explanation.definitionFit: To prise a lid off is to use a bar or tool to force it up.

clue.text: The French team pore over the dictionary

parts.note: le is French for the
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team
to con is to study carefully

explanation.surface: A French side studies a reference book closely.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is a word list or wordbook.

clue.text: Join up again to form retinue

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are used to form something new

explanation.surface: Followers regroup to make up a royal entourage.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring together once more is to unite after a separation.

clue.text: The relations of a benevolent leftist

parts.note: kind means benevolent
a Red is a left-winger, a communist

explanation.surface: A family tie to a generous socialist.
explanation.definitionFit: One's kin, those related by blood, are one's kindred.

clue.text: Ruling to infuriate retiring preservationists

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the word just before it is read in reverse

parts.note: to anger is to infuriate
the National Trust, NT, preserves Britain's historic buildings and landscapes

explanation.surface: A decision designed to annoy conservationists who are stepping down.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity looking after stately homes and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A regnant monarch is one actually reigning.

clue.text: A trick sure to go wrong

indicators.note: letters that go wrong are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A con certain to fail.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a deceptive stratagem.

clue.text: At one time it could offer a way out

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
taken as written

explanation.surface: Once upon a time something might have provided an escape route.
explanation.definitionFit: A door marked for leaving is an exit, a means of egress.

clue.text: Mount a little quiet nag

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone climbs onto a small, placid horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like the verb to get on a horse, but it is the volcano in Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a mountain, a volcano on Sicily.

clue.text: An excrescence calling for back-massage, right?

indicators.note: back means returned, so the word for massage is read in reverse

parts.note: to rub is to massage

explanation.surface: A lump or knot that calls for a massage of the back, surely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-massage' looks like one compound; 'back' is the reversal signal on RUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A burr is a rough knob or outgrowth on a tree, an abnormal growth on the surface.

clue.text: The girl having to live on a boat

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on top of another comes first

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
SS, steamship, is a boat

explanation.surface: A young woman has to live aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Bess is a girl's name, short for Elizabeth.

clue.text: Women who work with a will

definitions.text: Women who work with a will

parts.words: Women who work with a will
parts.note: reads as women working with determination, but means women charged with carrying out a dead person's testament

explanation.surface: Women who labour enthusiastically.
explanation.definitionFit: These are female executors, appointed to carry out the terms of a testament.

clue.text: An order not requiring attention

parts.note: sounds like a casual request, but is the parade-ground command that releases soldiers from standing stiffly

explanation.surface: An instruction that nobody need take notice of.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the drill command allowing soldiers to relax from the rigid attention position.
